subject: Transportation Systems
title: Inside a Container Ship
description: A 60-second lesson on Inside a Container Ship.

hook.text: The largest container ships carry 24,000 boxes. Laid end to end, they'd stretch 90 miles.

buildup.text: Containers stack 10 high in the hold and another 11 on deck, guided by cell rails and twist locks.

discovery.text: A crew of just 20 to 25 sailors operates a ship carrying $1 billion worth of cargo.

twist.text: The bridge sits at the stern because containers block forward visibility. Cameras fill the blind spot.

climax.text: These ships are longer than the Eiffel Tower is tall and wider than a highway is long.

punchline.text: Twenty-five people move a billion dollars across an ocean.

quiz.question: How many crew members typically operate a massive container ship?
